source_document.title: SOP Manual – Wastewater Treatment Plant: Liquid, Sludge and Biogas Systems
source_document.approval_note: The approval table on page 1 is blank. Section 3 (page 2) states that all set points, alarm levels and operating ranges are typical values for a mid-size plant that must be verified against manufacturer data, design basis, discharge permit and local regulations before use.

extraction_rules: Every value below was copied from the cited page of SOP-MAN-000. Nothing was estimated.
Fields the manual does not state are recorded as the string NOT SPECIFIED.
The manual names parameters, not PLC/HMI alarm tags. The 'opslens_mapping' block records which OpsLens simulated tag was associated with each parameter and how confident that association is.
The manual does not define alarm deadbands or reset/clear conditions. 'verification_criteria' records the procedure's own recovery checks, which are NOT alarm reset conditions.

levels.meaning: Risk to life, environment or permit compliance now
Equipment or process degrading, likely to reach P1

rules: Acknowledge the alarm within the time in the Alarm Priority Convention (Section 6 of this manual).
Read the tag name, value, limit and time. Check related instruments to confirm the alarm is genuine and not a sensor fault.
Classify the alarm P1, P2 or P3.
For P1 and P2: inform the shift supervisor, then go to the location with a torch, gas monitor and radio.
Take the immediate safe action in the relevant process SOP.
If the value keeps moving toward the next limit, escalate to the supervisor and on-call maintenance.
Never disable, shelve or inhibit an alarm without the supervisor's written approval.
Record the alarm, action, outcome and time in the shift log.

interlocks_or_restrictions: Do not enter the wet well. Use SOP-GEN-002 if entry is unavoidable. (page 14)
Isolate the failed pump under SOP-GEN-001. (page 14)

limits.text: If the channel level reaches 1.8 m (overflow weir), the event becomes P1.

limits.text: If the blanket exceeds 2.0 m, increase WAS withdrawal temporarily ... to the process engineer's instruction.

limits.name: WEIR / P1
limits.text: If the blanket reaches 2.5 m or effluent TSS reaches 30 mg/L, the event is P1.

definitions.alarm_tag_in_pdf: SLUDGE BLANKET HIGH (alarm name in text, page 20)
definitions.priority: NOT SPECIFIED below 2.5 m; P1 at 2.5 m (page 20)
definitions.acknowledgement: Acknowledge the SLUDGE BLANKET HIGH alarm. Check the actual blanket depth with the probe, then confirm with a manual sample. (page 20)
verification_criteria: Reduce the temporary flow limit gradually and watch the blanket fall below 0.8 m. This normally takes 4 to 8 hours. (page 20)

limits.name: ESCALATION
limits.text: If effluent TSS reaches 25 mg/L or turbidity reaches 10 NTU, inform the Plant Manager.

definitions.priority: Escalate at 25 mg/L (SOP-BIO-001 p.18); P1 at 30 mg/L (SOP-BIO-002 p.20)
verification_criteria: Sample the effluent hourly until TSS is back below 15 mg/L. (page 20)

opslens_mapping.note: Final effluent TSS (shared by the foam and RAS incidents).

limits.name: RELIEF
limits.action: If pressure reaches 38 mbar and the flare is not burning, or the relief valve is venting, the event is P1. (page 23)

definitions.alarm_tag_in_pdf: GAS HOLDER PRESSURE HIGH (alarm name in text, page 22)
definitions.priority: NOT SPECIFIED at 32 mbar; P1 at 38 mbar if flare not burning or relief venting (page 23)
definitions.acknowledgement: Acknowledge the siren and the GAS HOLDER PRESSURE HIGH alarm. Inform the shift supervisor. (page 22)
verification_criteria: Confirm the flare closes and holder pressure returns to 15 to 25 mbar. (page 23)
interlocks_or_restrictions: Do not override a flame-failure trip and do not bypass any gas safety interlock. (page 22)

definitions.parameter: Confined space atmosphere (O₂ / LEL / H₂S / CO)

normal.text: Oxygen 19.5 to 23.5 %; Flammable gas below 10 % LEL; H₂S below 10 ppm; CO below 25 ppm

verification_criteria: Re-test the atmosphere at least every 2 hours and after any break. (page 8)
interlocks_or_restrictions: Leave immediately if: O₂ below 19.5 % or above 23.5 %; 10 % LEL or above; H₂S 10 ppm or above; CO 25 ppm or above. (page 7)

known_gaps: The manual does not list PLC/HMI alarm tag names, alarm deadbands, on/off delays, or reset/clear conditions for any alarm.
The manual does not assign a P1/P2/P3 priority to individual alarm limits, except where an escalation clause states the event becomes P1.
All numerical values are 'typical values for a mid-size plant' (page 2) and the approval table (page 1) is blank.
